language_task: Pick up one object from the big bowl and put it inside the small box that is empty.
outcome_evidence: No bowl-to-box transfer is visible in this window. Instead, the robot acquires and repeatedly moves the orange box beside the bowl (left and top, frames 1423–1749), while the brown and green objects remain in the bowl (right, frames 1400, 1500, 1600 and 1749). This is a provisional window outcome: completion is unconfirmed, and earlier and later execution are unavailable; the visible local failure is prolonged box handling rather than a failed acquisition of a bowl object.

failure_annotations.explanation: The fingers close onto the orange box around frames 1423–1425 (left), after which the box moves with the arm away from the bowl, back toward it, and away again through frame 1749 (top; left shows the retained empty box). This prolonged back-and-forth box-handling sequence does not acquire or transfer any bowl object; the contents remain visible in right at frames 1500, 1600 and 1749. Although positioning a destination box could be useful preparation, the repeated transport here produces no discernible transfer progress. This segment is supported by the current images independently of the prior prediction; its continuation beyond the window is unknown.
failure_annotations.recovery: Set the box upright in an accessible location, release it, then select and grasp an object inside the bowl, verify retention, and transfer it into the empty box; no human intervention is visibly required.
failure_annotations.severity_evidence: The box remains retained, and no damage, spill, dropped object or harmful collision is visible in left, right or top through frame 1749.
failure_annotations.resetability_evidence: No environmental repair or human reset is indicated; the robot can set down the held box and proceed with the accessible bowl contents.
